The tannaitic Dostai entry explicitly distinguishes his father from the teacher of Rabbi Yochanan. The Eruvin mishnah has Dostai son of Yannai reporting in Rabbi Meir’s name. This supports the distinct chronological problem without settling Elazar’s parentage.

The entry places the father and sons in the tannaitic era. Dostai’s teaching in Meir’s name is explicit; the full synchronization with Akiva and the identification of Elazar as his brother remain the compiler’s argument.
Tosafot distinguishes the amora Rabbi Yochanan from a Rabbi Yochanan named in a Nazir baraita. Heilprin invokes that distinction as a possibility.
The separate Yochanan dossier discusses the exact view in Tosafot, including the tension between different occurrences.
The compiler expressly leaves the identification open. A shared burial tradition provides no independent proof of the suggested identification.
